character.lede: An oxblood-brick house sits under one steep bronze roof that steps down past a glass-roofed link to a low garage. A two-storey glazed slot, a light-blue entry bay and a gravel forecourt with topiary face the street.

spots.line: A club chair, a bookshelf and the Core on a desk.
A workbench and a bicycle fill the garage beyond the glass link.
Two sofas and a slipper chair gather round a trunk table.

facts.style: 1.5-storey oxblood-brick house under one steep bronze standing-seam roof that steps down west past a glass-roofed link to a low garage; a two-storey black-framed glazed slot notched into the front slope, a light-blue recessed entry bay with a black glazed pair, a gravel forecourt with a rock-edged sweep bed and cloud-pruned topiary

character.truths: The Core sits on a desk in the Den. There is no television: never say TV. The kitchen has an island. Patio with a fire bowl, gravel forecourt, topiary.

details.rule: every beat of an adult or teen persona (13 or older) gets a detail (before, after, steps, fact); pair beats first

nextcloud: [note] The Hub onboarding wizard offers Nextcloud as a recommended app.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
twenty: marketplace: QA capture shows real company names and logos.
drawio: Stateless: diagrams live in the browser or as .drawio files on the person's own device. The Core serves the editor only, so never say the diagram sits on the Core.
Listing says nothing else phones home: leave it.
QA screenshot is a blank editor.
forgejo: [note] Gitea does the same job. Name one Git host per household, not both.
[note] The listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI. The package ships the forge and its database only, no runner, so do not show a CI run.
[claims] Say where the repositories are (on the Core). Do not say it syncs with, or is compatible with, GitHub.
Listing says "fully self-hosted and private": over-claim, do not repeat.
Listing mentions Forgejo Actions CI, but no runner ships: never show a CI run.
calibre-web: [qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
marketplace: Documented default admin credentials (admin / admin123); no QA capture.
lunalytics: Setup wizard asks for email and username on first visit
Do not claim a public status page
Overlaps Uptime Kuma (another slice): one uptime monitor per household
wallos: [note] Fetches logos for popular services from outside.
homehub: No passwords: a "Select your user" box offers every name including Administrator (anyone on the network can pick one)
Extras bundled: recipes, expiry tracker, link shortener, PDF compressor, QR generator
open-notebook: [cloud-link] Supports 18 plus providers including cloud ones. Ollama is the local path.
[heavy] Podcast-style audio overviews need a speech model.
Install form has OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Groq key fields: leave blank; Ollama is the local path.
Podcast style audio overviews need a speech model: do not mention.
Capture shows sample notebook content, not personal data.
linkwarden: Sharing links publicly needs inbound reach: keep the story to saving, not sharing
The Pocket name in replaces is stale
jupyterlab: [note] One password set at install. The notebook kernel runs the code on the Core; installing a Python package reaches the internet.

[claims] Neither the manifest, the live store nor the Portal alternatives table (origin/main) names anything it replaces, so there is no replaces chip. The CI-Common campaign reference says MATLAB or RStudio, from a sour
QA screenshot is the token and password wall: reject.
Logo file shows only the orange arcs, not the Jupyter wordmark.
home-assistant: [hardware] The Hub package runs without privileged host mounts. Integrations that need direct USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access (a Zigbee stick, for example) are not enabled by default.
[note] Ships with a Matter server container alongside. Its manifest sets host_access true because that container uses host networking; no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted.
[claims] Do not promise energy savings. Home Assistant has no energy figures in the listing.
Matter container uses host networking (host_access true); no USB, Bluetooth or D-Bus access is granted, so no Zigbee stick.
The QA capture is the onboarding page (shows the product, no data).
comfyui: [amd-gpu] Built for AMD Ryzen AI Max (Strix Halo) with ROCm, the same family as the Core. Needs /dev/kfd and /dev/dri. No speed or model-fit claims beyond the fact sheet table.
Built for AMD Strix Halo with ROCm: needs /dev/kfd and /dev/dri (the Core family).
First start needs the internet to clone ComfyUI-Manager; checkpoints must be added by the household from outside sources.
No speed or model fit claim beyond the sheet.
invoice-ninja: [cloud-link] Taking card payments needs a payment provider. Say invoicing, not payment processing.
minio: Developer plumbing: the story needs a script or app using buckets.
Do not frame a bucket on the Core as an off-site backup.
cyberchef: Listing says nothing pasted is ever sent anywhere and that it works with no internet connection: do not repeat either (sec-never-leaves, sec-offline)
A tool, not a store of anything: nothing is held after the tab closes
samba: [note] No web interface; protocol only. Not useful as an on-screen hero.
[qa] No QA screenshot on origin/main (e2e/screenshots). It is listed and installable, but nobody has recorded a verified run.
Headless: no web interface, so nothing to show on a screen
Do not call it a NAS or a file server box
quarkdown: Pinned to a Linux x64 release while the manifest lists arm64 too (verify).
No QA screenshot; the listing image is a sample page.
The listing says local-first: files stay in the app data directory.
super-productivity: by default tasks live in the browser local storage, not on the Core
no sync means no custody on the Core
cryptgeon: Notes live only in RAM: a restart of the app wipes every unread note
Do not repeat the listing's encryption wording (sec-absolute); say a note opens once and is gone
Overlaps Enclosed and PrivateBin: one burn-after-reading tool per household
lubelogger: Do not claim savings or economy figures
No sign-in until the user sets one (unverified)
bentopdf: Dual licence: AGPL-3.0 or paid commercial; fine for household use
Listing says "nothing to leak": drop that wording
librephotos: [note] First setup takes 5 to 10 minutes while models and migrations start.
[note] No API is mentioned in the listing; treat as web interface only for agent purposes.
Face recognition is sensitive: say what it does, never that it "knows" people
Overlaps Immich; use it to relieve Immich's share
monetr: marketplace: Replaces lists Mint, which Intuit retired in 2024.
marketplace: Licence is the Functional Source License (not open source).
airtrail: Logbook and statistics, not live flight tracking (listing short_desc says "flight tracking")
Does not claim live flight status; story must say logbook
